p.i: liberatum ac reducem uideret in Germania. Soldanus ergo Imperatorem muneribus ornauit, uiatico profequit, 34. equis & certis militibus Brixiam usq; deduxit, ibiq; subsistit.

main_text.p: Principes de Imperatoris reditu certiores fi­ĕi, frequentes eum adibant. Cæsar Soldano suos varijs donis onustos remisit, adiunctis illis qui eos deducerent, usq; ad Imperij fines. Deinde comitia indixit Norimbergæ, & illuc vocabat omnes imperij principes: quibus Alexandri pontificis prodi­tionem aperuit, proditoriam epistolam ab eo ad Soldanum missam legit, & quibus modis liber esset dimissus expofuit. Principes pollicebantur illi auxilium, ut fidem suam apud Soldanum liberaret: indignantes & suppetias spondebant aduersus Alexandrum, Imperij proditorem. Conscribebatur exercitus: per Italiam nemine repugnante, Romam mouebat. Missisq; in urbem legatis suis, à Romano populo postulabat (dissimulata interim priuata iniuria) ut causa utriusq; Pontificis audita, restitueretur concordia ecclesiæ: decerneretur q;Papalis sedes uni ex electis Pontificibus, ut ecclesiasticæ administrationis summa penes unum maneret. Id uero si faceret, promisit se eis non solum pacem concessurum esse, sed etiam omnia reddituram, quæ iure debebantur. Alexander cernens Im
[The word "perato" at the lower right is the catchword and is not part of the text.]

page.notes: Long s printed as s throughout; st ligature in "adminiftrationis" and "fuppetias" read as "st"/"ss" as printed. The word "decerneretur" is followed by a printed ornament (q;) which is transcribed as "q;" with a doubtful reading. The line "Alexander cernens Imperato" is the last full line; "perato" is the catchword at the foot. Some ligatures and abbreviations (e.g. "&", "q;") are kept as printed. Words such as "Sol-danus" are written whole, as no hyphen is printed.
